DM5.period: Apr-Jun 2026: CCEP +3.2% (days-adjusted), Coca-Cola HBC +5.8% (underlying), Coca-Cola FEMSA +3.5%

lead: Coca-Cola is Building history (today's zone: Hold), at +26 on a −100 to +100 scale, up from +19 on 5 Oct and 4 points below the Buy line, mainly because the valuation score eased from −100 to −76 now that its price/earnings ratio vs its own 5-year history is scored (neutral), with demand edging up from +60 to +62 as the revenue-growth trend scores bullish: demand and the price trend are strong, but investors already pay well above its peers for it.
bullets: Demand is strong, but sits on a knife-edge. Demand scores +62, up from +60: organic revenue grew 6.0% and unit case volume 5.0% in the June quarter vs a year earlier, and the three big Coca-Cola bottlers' volumes rose 4.2% on average (Apr-Jun vs a year earlier). Revenue growth now scores bullish at 12.1% vs a 1.8% average for the prior four quarters (+10.2 points); gross margin is neutral at 61.7% vs 61.1% a year earlier (+0.7 points; bullish at +1.0). Organic growth sits exactly on its +6% bullish line, and the June quarter had help from the World Cup campaign; at +5.9% the composite would drop to about +20. Analysts' 2027 profit forecast is up 1.2% in 90 days ($3.52 vs $3.48), short of the +3% line.

It is priced at a big premium to peers, not to its own past. Valuation scores −76, up from −100: investors pay 27% more per dollar of expected profit over the next 12 months than for the peer median (24.8x vs 19.5x forward P/E; it turns neutral below +25%), 175% more after allowing for growth (3.9 vs 1.4), and 50% more on EV/EBITDA (23.5x vs 15.6x). Against its own history it looks normal and now scores neutral: the P/E on the last 12 months' actual profit is 27.1x vs a 26.5x 5-year median (+2%). What it means for you: the price already assumes Coca-Cola keeps delivering; a miss on 27 Oct has more room to hurt than a beat has to help.

The money backdrop is slightly negative. Liquidity scores −13 (unchanged): the dollar index is 2.99 points higher than 20 trading days earlier, a headwind for a company that earns most of its revenue abroad. Fed odds moved 11.3 points towards cuts (1% cut, 17% rise now vs 4% and 31% a month earlier), not enough to count (the line is 15 points). Buying and selling volume is balanced (0.91x up-day vs down-day volume, last 20 trading days; 1.14x yesterday). Not scored but relevant: the US 10-year yield rose 0.46 points in a month to 5.27%, above KO's earnings yield of about 4.0% (chain C2).

The price trend is up, but cooling. Price scores +100 on slow measures: KO is 7.5% above its 200-day average (8.0% yesterday), its 50-day average is 9.8% above the 200-day, and it is 7.7 points ahead of its peers' average return over the last 3 months. On the day it slipped 0.39% to $86.17 vs +0.58% for the S&P 500, and over the last 5 trading days it slipped 0.8% while the S&P 500 rose 1.9%.

Not yet confirmed. Day 2 of the 10 trading days of history needed for a call (2 of 10 recorded; today reads Hold); coverage is now 100% of the weight left after removing DM3. Next big test: results on 27 Oct, where the stronger dollar, a tough organic-growth comparison and the fading World Cup boost are the risks. A pending US tax-court appeal (about $20bn exposure) is not scored but could move the stock.

evidence.t: KO fell 0.39% to $86.17 vs +0.58% for the S&P 500. A typical day for KO is about 1.3% either way (last 60 trading days), so no classification is triggered.

evidence.t: Over the last 252 trading days KO has moved slightly against the market (sensitivity to the S&P 500 of -0.23: it has tended to rise on days the market fell), consistent with money rotating into defensive stocks when tech sells off. Yahoo's longer-run 5-year figure is 0.32.

past.date: Tue 28 Jul 2026, before the US open
past.vs: Comparable EPS $0.97 vs $0.93 expected (+4%, Yahoo consensus), +11% vs a year earlier. Revenue $13.38bn vs about $13.17bn expected; +7% reported, +6% organic.
past.guide: 2026 organic revenue raised to about +5% (from 4-5%); comparable EPS growth raised to 9-10% (from 8-9%), including about a 3-point currency tailwind. Free cash flow about $12.4bn.
past.reaction: +5.0% on the day (close to close); +6.5% for the week vs +1.0% for the S&P 500.
take: Volume surge. Unit case volume +5% vs a year earlier; Coca-Cola credits its global FIFA World Cup campaign with part of the gain (the tournament ran 11 Jun-19 Jul, so it also helps Q3). Price/mix +2%; concentrate sales +4%.
Every region grew. Volume: Asia Pacific +8%, Bottling Investments +5%, EMEA +4%, Latin America +3%, North America +3%.
Margins up. Operating margin 34.9% vs 34.1% a year earlier; comparable 35.6% vs 34.7%.

Acquisitions and divestitures (including the CCBA sale, a 75% stake to Coca-Cola HBC, expected to complete by end-2026) take 2-3 points off 2026 reported revenue growth and about 1 point off EPS growth (Coca-Cola's 2026 guidance).
Calendar shift: Q4 2026 has six fewer days than Q4 2025, so reported Q4 growth will look weak.
past.impact: DM4a (organic +6%) and DM4b (volume +5%) both bullish; the World Cup boost will not repeat.

past.vs: Comparable EPS $0.86 vs $0.81 expected (+6%), +18% vs a year earlier. Revenue $12.47bn, above expectations; +12% reported, +10% organic (six extra days helped).
past.guide: Comparable EPS growth raised to 8-9% (from 7-8%), mainly a lower tax rate; organic revenue kept at 4-5%.
take: Volume +3%, up in every operating segment; North America +4%.
Price/mix +2%, held back 2 points by Easter timing and mix.
Gross margin down about 0.3 points on tea and coffee costs; operating margin up about 0.7 points.
New CEO: Henrique Braun succeeded James Quincey at the end of March 2026.
past.impact: Demand solid; the guidance raise drove the move.

next.date: Tue 27 Oct 2026, before the US open (evening in Singapore)
watch: Organic revenue vs the +6% line (DM4a): +6.0% in Q2 sits exactly on the line, and Q3 2025 was a tough +6% comparison. Consensus reported revenue growth is +3.9% vs a year earlier.
Volume (DM4b; line +3%): Q3 2025 was only +1%, an easy comparison, and the World Cup ran into July.
Currency: the dollar index is up about 3 points in a month; guidance assumes a 3-point tailwind (chain C1).
CCBA completion timing (Coca-Cola HBC says by end-2026).
Six fewer days than Q4 2025: organic and reported growth will look weak for calendar reasons.
Costa: the sale was shelved in Jan 2026 when bids fell short; watch for a write-down.

shareholder_notes: Berkshire Hathaway holds 400m shares (9.3% of shares outstanding), unchanged; it is the largest holder and is not an index fund.
Nasdaq still lists an old Vanguard Group line dated 31 Dec 2025, from before Vanguard split its reporting; it is left out as stale.

Insider activity over the last 6 months is all selling (about $157m), led by chairman and former CEO James Quincey's $98.8m. The Form 4 filings for Quincey and Pietracci say the sales were under pre-arranged Rule 10b5-1 plans, largely to cover tax on vesting shares (SEC Form 4; MarketBeat, 30 Jul 2026).

Vanguard appears as several entities (Vanguard Capital Management, Vanguard Portfolio Management, Vanguard Fiduciary Trust) after it split its reporting; together they hold about 360m shares (8.4% of shares outstanding).

chains.name: Strong dollar
evidence: Dollar index 101.83 at the 6 Oct close vs 98.84 twenty trading days earlier: +3.0%.
2026 EPS guidance (+9-10%) includes about a 3-point currency tailwind (Coca-Cola, 28 Jul); a stronger dollar since then puts that tailwind at risk at the 27 Oct results.

The dollar index is mostly the euro; Coca-Cola's bigger exposures (Mexican peso, Brazilian real and other emerging-market currencies) can move differently. The first read on the actual hit comes at the 27 Oct results.

chains.name: Bond yields squeeze the valuation
path: KO's bond-like valuation harder to justify
evidence: 10-year yield 5.27% at the 6 Oct close vs 4.81% twenty trading days earlier: +0.46 points.
KO's dividend yield is about 2.5% of the share price and its earnings yield (inverse of the 24.8x forward P/E) about 4.0%, both below the 5.27% on the 10-year.

chains.name: Oil and aluminium costs
path: bottlers squeezed, less room for price rises
evidence: Brent $100.32 at the 5 Oct close vs $96.28 twenty trading days earlier: +4.2%, under the +10% line. It was $73.74 on 24 Jun 2026, so the rise since mid-year is large.
US Midwest aluminium premium now over 40% of the all-in aluminium price (Manufacturing Dive, 19 Aug 2026).

chains.name: Health rules on sugary drinks
path: SNAP soda bans, sugar taxes, GLP-1 drugs
evidence: At least 23 US states have approval to bar SNAP (food-stamp) money for soda; about 10 started in H1 2026 and about 20 by year-end. In the first 10, sugary-drink purchases by SNAP households fell 12% in H1 2026, and they did not switch to paying cash (Stanford/MIT/Chicago study, via Grocery Dive, 2 Sep 2026).
Numerator puts 2026 lost soda sales at up to $430m (29 May 2026), small vs Coca-Cola's $47.9bn revenue in 2025.
Mexico raised its tax on sugary drinks from Jan 2026; Coca-Cola FEMSA cited it for slightly lower Mexican volumes in H1 2026 (27 Jul 2026).
GLP-1 weight-loss drugs: outside estimates put about 12% of US adults on them, a drag of roughly 0.2% a year on US food and drink volume (OC&C, 2026).

defects: Staging build, second day of history: the call needs 10 trading days of scores before it can be confirmed.

SEC's data service returned no figures for Coca-Cola on 5 Oct 2026 (Apple's worked); the 6 Oct build now has them, so DM1 (revenue trend), DM6 (gross margin trend), VL3 (P/E vs own history), the quality & cash check and the free cash flow history are scored. Coverage is 100% of the weight left after removing DM3.
When SEC works again, stage B must read Coca-Cola's revenue under the tag 'Revenues' (it does not use the default revenue tag).

DM1 compares reported revenue growth, which bottler sales cut: acquisitions and divestitures (including CCBA) take 2-3 points off 2026 reported revenue growth (Coca-Cola guidance). DM4a (organic growth) carries the clean demand read (Kenneth, 5 Oct 2026).

DM4a (organic revenue growth) is +6.0% in the June quarter, exactly on its +6% bullish line: at +5.9% it would score neutral and the composite would fall to about +20. 'What would change the call' does not yet list DM4 and DM5 (engine).
DM5 (bottler volumes) is shown as a leading read, but the bottlers report a few days after Coca-Cola, so it confirms rather than leads.

DM4a, DM4b and DM5 are entered from results releases, so they update quarterly. DM5 averages three bottlers whose bases differ slightly (CCEP days-adjusted, Coca-Cola HBC underlying, Coca-Cola FEMSA reported).
Q2 2026 volume (+5%) was helped by the global FIFA World Cup campaign (11 Jun-19 Jul) and good weather in Europe; the boost fades from Q4 2026.

Free cash flow in the quality check is $12.6bn for the last 12 months to Mar 2026 (SEC), but the 2025 quarters include a one-off $6.1bn payment to fairlife's former owners in Q1 2025. Coca-Cola guides about $12.4bn for 2026. The quality check shows 1 flag of 5: cash conversion (operating cash ÷ net profit) of 64% and 57% over the last two years, below the 70% line.

Revenue mix: Asia Pacific (about 12% of revenue) sits in Other with corporate and the removal of sales between segments, because its filing tag changed between filings. Costa and innocent moved into EMEA from 1 Jan 2025 (2024 restated), so EMEA's 3-year comparison is not like-for-like, and the Dec 2023 quarter is wrong (EMEA about $4.45bn, Other negative): its fourth quarter is worked out from a restated full year minus quarters on the old basis. Open item for the Framework chat.
Institutional change (LQ3) counts changes in existing positions only.
Short interest (LQ2) is only 0.9% of freely traded shares, below the 2% minimum, so it scores neutral.

Not scored but material: Coca-Cola's US tax case (transfer pricing; about $20bn exposure, $6bn already deposited) awaits an appeals court ruling after the 25 Jun 2026 hearing; and the Costa coffee sale was shelved in Jan 2026, with a possible write-down.

Peer set (Kenneth, 5 Oct: brand owners only): Mondelez's 31% gross margin is closer to the bottlers that were excluded than to Coca-Cola's 62%. Without Mondelez, VL1 would read neutral (24.8x vs a 20.9x median, +19%) and the composite would be about +34, above the Buy line (+30). The zone is sensitive to this choice.

NA.sells: Concentrate to US and Canadian bottlers, plus finished drinks it makes itself (fairlife milk, juices, some fountain syrup).
NA.buyers: Coca-Cola's North American bottlers, restaurants and retailers.
pos: Largest part: 40.9% of revenue (last 4 quarters), up from 37.0% three years earlier.
Growing +7.0% (last 4 quarters vs the 4 before); +7.5% in the June quarter vs a year earlier.
neg: Margin 26.4% (last 4 quarters) vs 29.5% a year earlier, but only because of a one-off $960m BodyArmor trademark write-down in Q4 2025; without it the margin is about 31.1%, up about 1.6 points.
Most exposed to US health rules (SNAP soda bans, chain C4).

EMEA.sells: Concentrate to bottlers in Europe, the Middle East, Africa and India.
EMEA.buyers: Bottlers such as CCEP and Coca-Cola HBC.
pos: Growing fastest: +7.2% (last 4 quarters vs the 4 before).
Margin 37.5% (last 4 quarters), above the 32.1% figure for all segments together (which is itself held down about 2 points by the BodyArmor write-down).
neg: Only +2.0% in the June quarter vs a year earlier.
Most exposed to the dollar (chain C1) and to oil-driven costs and consumer strain from the Iran war (chain C3).

LATAM.sells: Concentrate to bottlers across Mexico, Brazil and the rest of Latin America.
pos: Highest margin: 60.4% segment operating margin (last 4 quarters), up from 58.0% three years earlier.
+15.9% in the June quarter vs a year earlier.
neg: Mexico's higher sugar tax (from Jan 2026) and lower Argentina volumes (Coca-Cola FEMSA, 27 Jul 2026).

BI.sells: Finished drinks from bottlers Coca-Cola still owns (mainly CCBA in Africa, plus India and parts of Asia).
pos: Margin improving: 8.8% (last 4 quarters) vs 7.3% a year earlier and 5.7% three years earlier.
neg: Shrinking by design: 12.0% of revenue vs 17.6% three years earlier; the CCBA sale (expected by end-2026) will cut it sharply.

shift.title: Coca-Cola is turning back into a pure concentrate business
pos: Bottling Investments fell from 17.6% to 12.0% of revenue in 3 years. The engine puts the margin gain from the change in mix at 3.1 points vs 3 years earlier, but much of that is an accounting artefact: Costa and innocent moved into EMEA from 1 Jan 2025 (2024 restated), which inflates EMEA's share. The gain from the bottler sales alone is smaller and not separately measured here.
The highest-margin regions (Latin America 60.4%, EMEA 37.5%) are growing at least as fast as the company (+6.5%, last 4 quarters vs the 4 before).
neg: Reported revenue shrinks with each bottler sale, so headline growth looks slower than the business: acquisitions and divestitures take 2-3 points off 2026 reported revenue growth (Coca-Cola guidance).
North America's reported margin dip (29.5% to 26.4%) is a one-off write-down, not a trend; excluding it the margin rose.
